title: Single-source computation of native derived internal Hom of Weil sheaves
statement:
Fix a finite field $k_0$, an algebraic closure $k$ of $k_0$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k_0)$, and $\Qlb=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Let $X$ be a $k_0$-scheme locally of finite type, put $\bar X=X\times_{k_0}k$, and let $\Phi=1_X\times\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$ for inverse $q$-power Frobenius $\gamma$ of $k$, where $q=\#k_0$. On a small representative of $\bar X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention], let $R$ be the ring sheaf whose sections on $U$ are continuous functions $|U|\to\Qlb$ whose values locally span a finite-dimensional $\mathbf Q_\ell$-subspace. Write $\mathcal A$ for the category of $R$-module sheaves $F$ with an isomorphism $\theta_F:\Phi^*F\xrightarrow{\sim}F$, and maps commuting with $\theta_F$ (fixed pairs [def-weil-endofunctor-fixed-pair-category] in the sheaf category). Use the native derived category $D(\mathcal A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], formed by inverting equivariant quasi-isomorphisms. Write $H(A,B)=\mathcal Hom_R(A,B)$ with structure $h\mapsto\theta_B\Phi^*(h)\theta_A^{-1}$, and $H_A=H(A,-)$. For an additive functor $H_A$, its total right derived functor $RH_A$ is computed by applying $H_A$ termwise to a K-injective representative. Here a complex $I$ is K-injective if every map from an acyclic complex to $I$ is null-homotopic. The native bifunctor $\operatorname{RHom}_{\mathrm W}(K,N)$ is the image of $H^\bullet(J,I)$ for the chosen K-injective representatives $J,I$ of $K,N$, with $H^\bullet(J,I)^n=\prod_p H(J^p,I^{p+n})$ and differential $d(f)=d_I f-(-1)^n f d_J$. Let $A\in\mathcal A$ be any sheaf, and let $N\in D(\mathcal A)$ have cohomology zero in all sufficiently negative degrees. Then there is a natural isomorphism in $D(\mathcal A)$
$$\operatorname{RHom}_{\mathrm W}(A[0],N)\xrightarrow{\sim}(RH_A)(N).$$
More precisely, for a K-injective representative $I$ of $N$ and a K-injective resolution $\alpha:A[0]\to J$, the isomorphism is represented by precomposition
$$QH^\bullet(J,I)\xrightarrow{\sim}QH^\bullet(A[0],I)=Q(H_A(I)),$$
and the rightmost object computes $(RH_A)(N)$. Here $Q$ is localization at quasi-isomorphisms. The comparison is independent of these choices and natural contravariantly in $A$ and covariantly in $N$. No lissity, dual, tensor product, or constructibility hypothesis on $A$ is imposed.

proof.text: Use the source library K-injective equivalence. For each complex K lift the inverse equivalence counit to a unique map eta_K in the homotopy category, using bijectivity of localization on maps into K-injectives. Apply the contravariant native product-Hom functor and the quotient comparison to construct comparison_K,I. Naturality follows from uniqueness of the lift. On a K-injective source it equals the source library bifunctorRHomOfComplexObjIso; for any quasi-isomorphism alpha to a K-injective J it equals RHom((Q alpha)^-1) followed by that iso and Q Hom(alpha,I).

Apply lem-sf-native-hom-precomposition-quasi-iso to an existing K-injective resolution of A[0]. Each factor of the resolution formula for comparison is invertible, so comparison_A[0],I is invertible. Compose with the proved source-degree-zero projection and the inverse rightDerivedFunctorObjQIso. This constructs c canonically, without choosing an arbitrary witness of the theorem being proved.

The formula in step 1 proves the normalization for every alpha. Projection commutes with single-source precomposition and target postcomposition, checked on product components. Combine comparison naturality with naturality of the right-derived unit on K-injectives, canceling the canonical isomorphism on the right. Transport along kInjectiveRepIso N to obtain the arbitrary-target clause. These calculations retain the native row sign; the projection is in source degree zero so its sign is +1.
